key_idea: Sign the edges of the hypercube so that the signed adjacency matrix squares to nI. Its spectrum is then ±√n, each with multiplicity half, and Cauchy interlacing forces any principal submatrix of size more than half to have top eigenvalue at least √n, which in turn bounds the maximum degree.
reason: A decades-old open conjecture is settled in a few lines: one clever signed matrix, a trace argument, interlacing and a trivial degree bound, with no cases and no computation. The only slight shortfall is that the reason this particular signing works feels like a discovered trick more than an inevitable one, but almost nothing could be removed.
recognized: Hao Huang's proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture (Annals of Mathematics, 2019)
